items.abstract: <jats:p>Large Language Models (LLMs) have become powerful tools capable of generating coherent text, answering complex questions, and performing multi-step reasoning across diverse applications, including natural language understanding, content generation, automated reasoning, and multimodal interactions. Despite their impressive capabilities, LLMs face challenges such as hallucinations, inconsistent or biased outputs, and difficulties in precise reasoning, highlighting the need for post-training interventions. Post-training is a critical stage that refines pre-trained models for task-specific adaptation, improved reasoning, factual accuracy, and alignment with human expectations. Key post-training approaches include: (1) fine-tuning, which updates model parameters using labeled or task-specific data to enable domain specialization; (2) alignment, which adjusts model behavior to better follow human preferences and values; (3) knowledge adaptation, which equips models with domainspecific knowledge for contextually relevant outputs; and (4) reasoning enhancement, which improves logical inference, multi-step problemsolving, and structured decision-making. These methods collectively enhance model reliability, consistency, and usability. The importance of post-training became particularly evident after the release of GPT-3, motivating research on efficient ways to improve large models without retraining from scratch. In this survey, we provide a unified perspective on the post-training lifecycle of LLMs, organizing existing methods under the four key aspects of fine-tuning, alignment, knowledge adaptation, and reasoning enhancement. We also discuss practical strategies for improving model performance and usability in real-world applications, addressing gaps left by prior surveys that largely focus on isolated techniques or reinforcement learning approaches.</jats:p>
title: A Survey of LLM Post-Training: Approaches to Training, Reasoning and Data Creation
